name: Anders Kristian Munk
title: Director
bio: Anders Kristian Munk is Professor of Computational Anthropology in the Section Science and Technology Studies at DTU Management. His research focuses on controversies about emerging technologies, particularly about artificial intelligence and the green transition. Over the past decade, he has worked to integrate computational methods into more qualitative traditions. In that capacity, he has co-founded the Public Data Lab, The Techno-Anthropology Lab, and MASSHINE (Aalborg University's hub for computational social science and humanities), the latter two of which he has also directed. He holds a D.Phil. in Geography from the University of Oxford and has been a senior visiting researcher at the SciencesPo médialab in Paris.

name: Anders Koed Madsen
title: Data, democracy, digital urbanism
bio: Anders Koed Madsen focuses on data, democracy, and digital urbanism, exploring the intersection of technology and social systems.

name: Tanja Schneider
title: Science and Technology Studies, market studies, digital food studies
bio: Tanja’s research examines how digital technologies shape, and are shaped by, everyday life, with a focus on food and ethical consumption. As a James Martin Fellow at the University of Oxford, she researched how civil society organizations and consumers use digital platforms to challenge food industry practices, contributing to key works such as Digital Food Activism (2018) and helping establish Digital Food Studies. She later led the FoodCoach project and co-founded the Digital Foodscapes Network, advancing interdisciplinary research on digital food technologies. Her work highlights both their transformative potential and their tendency to reinforce existing practices.

name: Johan Irving Søltoft
title: Data interventions, perspectival modelling, synthetic ethnography
bio: Johan Irving Søltoft is a committee member at ECHO LAB.
workingGroups: Games as Tools for Research and Engagement

name: Lasse Uhrskov Kristensen
title: Digital sovereignty, open source infrastructures, transnational code sharing
bio: Lasse Uhrskov Kristensen studies transnational code sharing between public sector organisations on GitHub, examining how code travels and transforms as it is adopted and forked across institutional contexts. Drawing on STS and digital methods, his work engages with debates on digital sovereignty, where open-source software is mobilised to reduce national dependencies — while simultaneously producing new ones. At ECHO, he also contributes to building and maintaining the observatory's research infrastructures and data pipelines.

name: Csilla Duray
title: Social Data Science, participatory urban planning, perspectival modelling
bio: Csilla Duray’s work focuses on engaging everyday public transportation users through the Urban Belonging App to learn about problems they encounter and what they find important. At ECHO, she explores how these citizen-perspectives can be represented by fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) and retrieval augmented generation (RAG) algorithms. Her research explores how generative AI can facilitate co-creation and scenario design and integrate public opinion into planning processes.
workingGroups: Games as Tools for Research and Engagement

name: Frederik Bay-Jørgensen
title: Computational anthropology, explainable AI, AI alignment
bio: In Echo, Frederik Bay-Jørgensen contributes to the development of methods for perspectival modelling using generative AI. He stays up to date with recent advances in small- to mid-sized open-source models and integrates them into observatorial pipelines for attending to technological questions in society. He also helps maintain the observatory’s computing setup, which enables the safe local use of AI in our work.
workingGroups: Games as Tools for Research and Engagement

name: Emma Veland
title: Committee
bio: Emma Veland is a committee member at ECHO LAB.

name: Daniel Nordstrand Frantzen
title: Valuation struggles, wind energy, planning controversies
bio: Daniel Nordstrand Frantzen is a qualitative researcher exploring issues and controversies related to the energy transition. He collaborates with ECHO on observing societal debates on technologies - mainly related to matters of energy and sustainability more broadly. Furthermore, he uses workshop methods and game design in his research.
workingGroups: Games as Tools for Research and Engagement

name: Benjamin Lipp
title: Digital health, AI & robotics, cocreation
bio: Benjamin Lipp is studying the social impact of digital technology and infrastructure on healthcare practices. He is interested in utilising participatory sensing approaches for studying digital care infrastructures. He is also steering efforts to utilise games and game design for research and cocreation purposes.
workingGroups: Games as Tools for Research and Engagement

name: David Anthony Charles Broomham
title: Committee
bio: David Anthony Charles Broomham is a committee member at ECHO LAB.

name: Andreas Rattenborg Holm-Hansen
title: AI, NLP, computational social science
bio: Andreas Rattenborg Holm-Hansen works with the development of AI-based tools and analytical workflows to investigate how technology and science are discussed in Danish media. His work spans data processing, language technology, and computational text analysis, as well as the visualization and communication of insights so that complex patterns and developments become understandable and applicable. In ECHO, he contributes both technically and analytically at the intersection of AI, media, and society.
